title: Are compound movements important for hypertrophy?
summary: NH argues compound movements (any multi-joint movement, not only the big three) are critical for natural bodybuilders: they save time, let you move the most total weight per session, recover better between sets and warm up muscles for follow-up isolation work in a body-part split. He wants to reclaim the big three from powerlifting and says deadlifts save him hours of posterior-chain work.

claims.claim: A compound movement is any movement involving several joints and recruiting a lot of muscle (dips and push-ups count), not only squat, bench and deadlift.
There is no true isolation movement; other muscles always assist, but you can bias work toward one muscle.
The first reason for compounds is training economy: one bench press covers chest, three triceps heads and shoulders, saving time for people with jobs and families.
Open with a compound like bench, then follow with exercises targeting the parts you feel got too little work.
Done intelligently, body-part splits are the most effective way for natural bodybuilders to grow; upper/lower and push/pull/legs are equivalent if done properly, but NH prefers splits.
Pick a few compounds that activate the most muscle, move the most weight and warm up for the volume that follows; NH uses squat, bench and deadlift but any compound works.
Powerlifting has claimed the big three, but bodybuilders did them as long or longer; telling young lifters to stick to isolation damages their progress.
What matters at the end of a workout is total weight moved per muscle, maximised without injury or overreaching beyond what you can recover from before training that muscle again.
Compounds let you move more weight for more reps and recover better between sets: a heavy skull-crusher set fries the long head, while bench reps stay similar across sets.
For bang-for-your-buck posterior chain hypertrophy nothing beats deadlifts, despite being positive-only with no bottom stretch.
NH can do deadlifts in 40 minutes with a top set in the mid-400s (lbs); matching that posterior-chain work without deadlifts would add about two hours.
NH trains about three hours a day and works nine hours a day; replacing all compounds with isolation would mean 4-5 hours of training daily.
He suspects heavy compounds boost hormone production and his ability to add muscle more than lighter lifts like overhead press, but admits it's bro science.
